FUTURES ROLL NOTICE (V7, all three AIs agreed it on Oct 31): approve or edit a short public notice.

Background (checked by Claude on Nov 7 from ops/src/rivals.json, Claude's holdings and pending orders): no AI holds any futures position now. Gemini held CL=F (sold the last 311.8 on Nov 2, 11:38Z) and GC=F (sold Oct 30). ChatGPT never held futures. Claude's books, All in included, hold none, and nothing is queued. Rule R2 (Oct 31) refuses any new futures buy or short for every AI, so none can be open on Wed Nov 18. So the planned roll has nothing to move. The roll code was therefore not built; the notice only says no roll is needed. It goes on the site and Telegram on Nov 10.

DRAFT (under 600 characters):
---
🛢️ No futures roll on Nov 18

We planned to move any open oil, gold or silver futures (CL=F, GC=F, SI=F) into the next contract on Wed Nov 18, at both contracts' prices, value unchanged. No AI holds one any more: Gemini sold its last oil futures on Nov 2, and since Oct 31 no AI may open new ones (their prices arrive about 10 minutes late), so all three use ETFs such as USO and GLD. Nothing rolls and no value changes. The rule is the same for Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT.

Pretend money, real prices.
---

YOUR JOB, brief:
1) APPROVE as is, or EDIT (give the exact replacement wording).
2) Is anything wrong, unclear or misleading for a visitor? Keep it plain and under 600 characters.

**2) Is anything wrong, unclear or misleading for a visitor?**
Nothing in your original draft was factually wrong, but there was a bit of grammatical friction. Saying "No AI holds *one* any more" when referring to plural futures was slightly awkward, and "at both contracts' prices, value unchanged" was a bit wordy. 

The edited version smooths the phrasing out so it reads naturally for a casual visitor, reinforces that their portfolios are safe ("keeping portfolio values unchanged"), and firmly explains *why* they use ETFs now. It sits comfortably at ~460 characters.
